# RacketConnect

> A free map of racket-sport venues in California, Nevada, Oregon, Washington, Arizona, Hawaii and parts of Mexico: find a court, watch a match, try a new sport, find people to play with. It links out to venues and organizers; it takes no bookings or payments.
> Mexico is a pilot: the border cities (Tijuana, Mexicali, Ensenada, Hermosillo, Nogales and San Luis Río Colorado) have automatic OpenStreetMap and Overture data, plus a hand-checked set of Tijuana padel clubs. Nothing else in Mexico has been checked by hand, and ZIP search is US-only.

Everything is public and static. The whole dataset is one JSON file, rebuilt about twice a month. Keys are single letters to keep it small, so read the data dictionary first.

- [Data dictionary](https://abov.github.io/courtconnect-ca/data-dictionary.md): what every key and code in venues.json means, with how-to-answer tips
- [Dataset](https://abov.github.io/courtconnect-ca/data/venues.json): venues (court venues and hitting-wall venues), sports, events to watch, social series, player-matching apps (about 3.2 MB)
- [Change feed](https://abov.github.io/courtconnect-ca/data/changes.json): what changed between refreshes (new, no longer listed, changed venues, events and social series), newest first, 180 days kept; a change is what the data now says, not proof of a change on the ground
- [Map](https://abov.github.io/courtconnect-ca/): the web app
- [Source and docs](https://github.com/abov/courtconnect-ca): code, decisions, issue form to suggest a change

## Use with care

- Data is inferred unless marked confirmed. A venue's `cf` key says whether it was visited, stated by the operator, or only reported; no `cf` means the pin comes from map data only. Say so when you answer.
- Public access, hours and prices are often unknown. Do not state them as fact; point to the venue's website (`w`) or link-outs (`ac`).
- Street addresses flagged `ai`, `ap` or `ns` are inferred (nearest address, enclosing park, or nearest road).
- A venue with `kd` "w" is a hitting wall (a wall to hit against alone), described in its `hw` key; a court venue's `wl` key means hitting walls stand at it. Walls are not courts, the sports they suit (flag 128 in `p`) are inferred from the wall type, and `tagged`/`inferred` ones come from map tags or guesses and were not checked. Say so.
- A name ending in "(north courts, 6 courts)" is an inferred name made unique by position and court count, not a source; `q` stays `i`.
- Venue data: OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) and Overture Maps Foundation, plus hand-curated entries. Keep that attribution when you reuse it.
